title: BHC Capital Planning and VaR Model Validation

maps.tested: Paired with MR Reading 6, Validating Bank Holding Companies' VaR Models, which the sheet flags as a new topic, highly testable.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'BHC'. Both readings are new or newly emphasised, which historically correlates with heavier sampling. Capital planning governance, scenario design, and the validation standards applied to BHC VaR models are the examinable content.

vardeezReading: ORR-20: Important. MR-6: Important, with the note "New Topic - Highly Testable" ("New topic, highly testable").

selectors.name: Capital planning governance, board versus management
selectors.what: Who does what in a BHC's capital adequacy process: the board has ultimate oversight, approves the capital plan and capital decisions and receives capital information at least quarterly (including post-stress pro forma measures); senior management implements, ensures scenarios are severe enough, recommends goals and distributions and reports weaknesses. Also the reporting of management overlays: the board must see both the initial results and the results after judgmental adjustments, and extensive overlays should trigger a model review. Includes the Capital Plan Rule scope (US top-tier BHCs with USD 50 billion or more in assets) and the seven principles of an effective capital adequacy process where the point is governance and oversight.

selectors.name: BHC scenario design and estimation practices
selectors.what: Which scenario-design and estimation practices the Federal Reserve calls stronger or weaker: a BHC-designed scenario must reflect the firm's own vulnerabilities, a generic recession or a mirror of the supervisory scenario is weak, and neither leading practices nor results better than the supervisory scenario are a safe harbor. Also the loss, revenue and balance sheet estimation methods (long-run average PD, LGD and EAD are not appropriate for stress; net charge-off models and scalars are not primary tools for material portfolios; PPNR, balance sheet and RWA must tell one coherent story; no favourable management actions that cannot be assured).

selectors.name: Validation standards for BHC VaR models
selectors.what: The three validation components (conceptual soundness, outcomes analysis, benchmarking) applied to BHC VaR models. Conceptual soundness: VaR must show how risk changes when positions change, so a GARCH VaR on actual P&L can be more accurate yet not fit for purpose. Sensitivity analysis: component and marginal VaR from the Euler decomposition, and the challenge of missing position history and proxies. Confidence intervals: asymptotic standard error needs the density at the VaR, order-statistic and bootstrap alternatives, intervals are asymmetric, HS intervals are widest in stress and FHS intervals narrowest. Benchmarking: the most neglected component, why it is hard, a GARCH(1,1) VaR on the bank's own P&L as a ready benchmark, and the regulatory loss function (favours conservatism, positional VaR wins) against the check loss (rewards accuracy, P&L VaR wins at 16 of 19 banks).

notSelected: ORR-20 a and b beyond governance, scenario design and estimation (the detail of risk identification, internal controls, capital policy goals and targets, contingency planning) and the choice of VaR method (historical simulation, GARCH, filtered historical simulation) and the backtesting tests of outcomes analysis (see C2) are not separate selectors; no Vardeez pointer or Map point names them.
